Describe the cohort, with denominators and missingness

Source: R/eda.R
mm_eda.Rd

A Table 1 in tidy form: one row per variable level or statistic, overall and by outcome, with the denominator each percentage is taken over and the missing count beside it.

Usage

mm_eda(cohort, by = NULL, vars = NULL, digits = 1)

Arguments

cohort

A data frame, or a mm_clean() result.

by

Optional column to stratify by, typically the outcome.

vars

Columns to describe. Defaults to all but by.

digits

Decimal places for continuous summaries.

Value

An object of class mm_eda, holding table and missing.

Details

Missingness travels with the description rather than in a separate table, because a percentage whose denominator excludes missing rows reads as a fact about the cohort when it is a fact about the rows that happened to be complete.

Formatting follows the specification: counts with thousands separators, percentages to one decimal, means with standard deviations, medians with the quartiles.

No dependency on a table-rendering package. This returns a data frame, so gt, gtsummary, knitr::kable() or Quarto can render it, and none of them is needed to compute it.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 1)
mm_eda(cohort, by = "event", vars = c("age", "bmi", "sex"))
#> <mm_eda>  300 rows, by event
#>       variable         statistic           Overall         event = 0
#>  (denominator)                 n               300               272
#>            age         mean (SD)       62.4 (12.5)       62.4 (12.4)
#>            age median (p25, p75) 61.5 (54.3, 70.8) 61.5 (54.3, 70.8)
#>            age    missing, n (%)          0 (0.0%)          0 (0.0%)
#>            bmi         mean (SD)        29.0 (6.2)        28.9 (6.1)
#>            bmi median (p25, p75) 28.8 (24.8, 33.1) 28.7 (24.8, 32.9)
#>            bmi    missing, n (%)          0 (0.0%)          0 (0.0%)
#>            sex     female, n (%)       221 (73.7%)       201 (73.9%)
#>            sex       male, n (%)        79 (26.3%)        71 (26.1%)
#>            sex    missing, n (%)          0 (0.0%)          0 (0.0%)
#>          event = 1
#>                 28
#>        62.8 (14.0)
#>  61.1 (55.8, 70.0)
#>           0 (0.0%)
#>         29.5 (7.5)
#>  29.1 (25.5, 35.5)
#>           0 (0.0%)
#>         20 (71.4%)
#>          8 (28.6%)
#>           0 (0.0%)
